questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to expand my academic knowledge on Japanese Film and society, and get a better understanding of intercultural communication.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The Japanese are very helpful and want to help regardless of their English skills, so asking in the airport or reaching out to people was fairly easy. + The university also provided help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival we had a guide from the USTEP or Global office, which provided us with insights and knowledge on everyday life in Japan and the steps we needed to take in order to move in to accommodation and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several different options, some closer to campus and some further away. I chose accommondation at Komaba Lodge, which is close to Kamaba campus were I had the most of my courses, but other options were located closer to Hongo, so keep that in mind when signing up for the lottery.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a common kitchen, but there was no pots or pans, so please bring or purchase these items if you would like to cook at the dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is super convenient and you will meet a lot of wonderful people from all over the world, who is eager to go explore Japan with you!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A link was provided to a webpage were you will out a registration. This was fairly easy, but make sure to collect all the needed data in prior, so that there will be no issues with your application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Serval emails were provided if you had any questions regarding the registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in getting into all the classes I wanted, but please note that the globe program courses only have few studens - often below 20, so sign up as early as possible to make sure you get the courses you really want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read through the course catalog easily to get some inspiration for which courses you would like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels were easier but, I also had a lot of courses compared to KU. Here I usually have two that are fairly heavy and in Japan I had ate, which varied in level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The overall teaching style was very different depending on the course and the expectations the individual professor had. This is all bought to the attention of the students pretty early on - so make sure you don't load up on all the heavy courses but take various different level ons, so it doesn't tak up all you time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: The Kitchen supply that I had to go out and purchase - even though I thought it would be provided.

questions.answer: The far traveling - if by train is pretty expensive I would suggest to use the bus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really attend any clubs, but I went to the gathering that was hosted by the Global tutors.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So there would be bon-bon parties and onigiri cooking classes - and other gatherings to get to know each other and befriend the local students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would suggest for a trip to Hiroshima to learn about the history that Japan suffered after WWII

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Don't go to the super touristy parts, since they will be filled - but go on little hicks in the areas around them - and you can really find some hidden gems.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty thought not knowing the language, so that you can communicate with the locals - so I would suggest to take the courses and practice. Overall it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would suggest you ask them for their advice on what to see in Tokyo or Japan - and ask them to join your day trips. - and attend the Go Tutors events to meet the local students who are interested in International students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the overall approachability, the Japanese seems a little closed off in the beginning, but give them time and get to know them, and there will be true and great friendships there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that everything runs so smoothly - the trains on time and that everyone is super polite towards each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for more courses then you need and drop the additional ones, once you know which ones you get. 
Don't be afraid to ask a local student if they would like to hang out or do something together - for the most part they will say yes. 
Be open towards the Japanese culture and the people there - and share your own culture with them - so bring some snacks so they can learn about Denmark - they really are just as interested in you as you are in them :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to reach out to the institution and ask them anything - they are quite good at replying quickly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships that I made and the overall new cultural appreciation I have for other people - who might experience the world differently, but still have a lot in common with me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting back into a more heavily course load, where you have serval different courses which may be about very different things - so it requires a lot of studying - but you also learn a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
